SMTO-FIL-0028 — A folder link loops back on itself

GUID: 363fc88b-ec70-4cc6-8b03-8effc4f4b918
Slug: file-symlink-cycle
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO stopped following a path because a link (a shortcut to another folder) leads back into a folder it had already gone through. If you asked for a list or search, files inside that loop are left out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO again, giving the folder's real location rather than a path that passes through a linked or shortcut folder. The real location has no loop, so SMTO can open it normally.
  2. If you look after that computer, find the link named in Technical details and change it so it no longer points to a folder that contains it. A link pointing back up to its own parent folder is what creates the endless loop.
  3. If it still stops, open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The details show exactly which path contains the loop.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens, lists or searches the folder without this message, and the results include the files you expected.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't ask anyone to turn off SMTO's folder protections to get past this; avoid or fix the looping link instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway File operation stopped because path resolution hit a symbolic-link loop (ELOOP or a resolver RuntimeError), or directory traversal re-entered an ancestor directory with the same device/inode identity.

What this means

  • Path resolution raised a symlink-loop error or traversal encountered a directory identity already visited. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Path resolution raised a symlink-loop error or traversal encountered a directory identity already visited.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the link chain and visited directory identity; repeated traversal identity need not prove a broken target file.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, inspect the path from the receipt's path context with ls -l and readlink -f (or dir /AL on Windows) and repoint or remove the symlink that resolves to its own ancestor, or request a path that does not traverse it. List/search record the cycle as incomplete coverage (symlink_cycle) instead of following it; do not disable execution.path_boundary or other path guards.
  • Correct the cyclic link or choose a noncyclic path; keep path protections enabled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended noncyclic path can be traversed within the accepted scope.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
